conversation.content: Fernando is a soil sensor that texts you, in your plant's voice, when it needs water or light. It costs $49 once. Would you buy one? Be honest.
Forty-nine bucks is a week of groceries for me, so not alone. But if my roommates split it? Probably yes. We're all killing the same pothos.
Have you split the cost of something for the apartment before? How did that go?
Yeah, we Venmo'd for an air fryer in September. Took three weeks to collect, but we did it. A plant that roasts us in the group chat would sell itself to them.
Fernando is a soil sensor that texts you, in your plant's voice, when it needs water or light. It costs $29 plus $3 a month. Would you buy one? Be honest.
I'd think about it as a gift, but three dollars a month means I'm gifting someone a bill. That feels rude.
Who would you be buying it for?
My sister. She kills a plant a season. I'd happily pay fifty up front so she never sees a charge from me in her statement.

Honestly? Yes. Maybe two. My roommate is my watering system and she's moving out in June. A plant that texts me in a dramatic voice is exactly how my brain works.
What would make you pick this over setting phone reminders?
Reminders are me nagging me, and I ignore me. If the monstera texts 'I am PARCHED, Lena' I'll laugh and actually go water it.

What do you do today when one of the plants looks unhappy?
Give it more water. If it dies, my wife buys another one for twelve bucks. That's cheaper than a year of your subscription.

Maybe one, for the calathea, which is the only plant that beats my system. Forty-nine is fine for hardware. Is the data exportable?
What would it have to do that your self-watering pots don't already?
Light and humidity. The pots handle water. If it told me the calathea's corner drops below 40% humidity, that's worth fifty dollars. The jokes are optional.

For the grandkids, maybe. They kill every violet I give them. But not with a monthly fee. I'm not paying for my grandson's plant until he's thirty.

They don't. That's the whole problem. If it texted me the night before a trip, 'water me before you go,' that would actually save the plant.

What happened with the plant you lost most recently?
Gerald. Fiddle leaf fig. I had an alarm for him and swiped it away for two weeks during a launch at work. He dropped every leaf in one weekend. I'm still not over it.
